newsitem.title: USA: Wal-Mart begins tender for Cifra shares.
newsitem.headline: Wal-Mart begins tender for Cifra shares.

text.p: Wal-Mart Stores Inc, the No. 1 U.S. retailer, said Friday it had begun a tender offer for certain shares of Cifra SA de CV, Mexico's largest retailer.
The offer is being made under a merger deal announced in June under which two Wal-Mart/Cifra joint ventures will be merged into Cifra.
Wal-Mart expects to own a controlling interest in Cifra if the merger deal is consummated and the tender offer is successful, the U.S. retailer said in a statement.

Wal-Mart is offering to buy a total of 593.1 million series A and series B common shares of Cifra at US$2.03 cash each, or about US$1.2 billion. The offer price is payable in the Mexican peso equivalent or in U.S. dollars, at the option of the tendering shareholder.
The offer to buy the shares is being made by a Mexican trust formed by Wal-Mart.
The dealer-managers for the offer are Goldman Sachs Mexico Casa de Bolsa and Acciones y Valores de Mexico SA de CV.
The offer expires at noon Meico City time/1300 EDT/1700 GMT August 22. The trust is not obligated to buy shares that are not validly tendered.
The offer cannot be extended without the approval of the Mexican National Banking and Securities Commission.
